full_judgment:
3. The learned District and Sessions Judge Bakergonj, held an enquiry by starting 3 contempt cases, examined witnesses, got documents exhibited and thereafter submitted report to this court on the basis of which the present Rule was issued. 

 We will now consider the cases of the individual contemnors separately. 

 First we will take up the case of Advocate Abdul Majid Munshi. In the affidavit filed by him he has denied the allegations and stated his own version of the case. He has also filed a supplementary affidavit on 24.1.80 annexing some documents. 

 7. As regards the filing of the plaint of Money Suit No. 3 of 1980 in the 2nd Court or Munsiff, Barisal, the admitted position is that the plaint was filed through Advocate Maniruddin Talukder. There is no evidence to link up Opposite Party No. 2 Advocate Abdur Rab with the filing of the said Money suit. There is, however, unimpeachable evidence for coming to the conclusion that Opposite Party No. 1 Abdul Majid Munshi has been the architect behind the Money Suit. Mr. Nurul Islam (P.W.23) Deputy Jailor of Barisal Jail. has proved that Opposite Party No. 1 Abdul Majid Munshi obtained signatures of Abul Kalam on the plaint (Ext. 27) and vokalatname (Ext. 4) in his presence and he attested those signatures under his official seal. Exhibits and witnesses referred to in this judgment are exhibits and witnesses examined by the District Judge, in contempt case No. 1 of 1980. P.W. 23 has further proved the Opposite Party No. 1 produced before him a permission of the A.D.C. granted on an application alleged to have been filed by Abul Basher, brother of Abul Kalam P.W. 17. Aminul Hoque Chowdhury, an advocate practising in Barisal Bar has proved that the application (Ext, 91 is in the handwriting of Opposite Party No. 1, who has made an endorsement in the application in his own hand that the petitioner was known to him and signed is his presence. The Deputy Jailor Mr. Nurul Islam has also proved that the name, father's name and address of Abul Kalam at the top of the Vokalatnama were written by Opposite Party No. 1 in his presence. 

 8. The next evidence to connect Opposite Party No. 1 Abdur Mazid Munshi with the filing of the suit is the evidence of Mr. Mainul Hasan (P.W.16), staff reporter of "Biplobi Bangladesh" a weekly of Barisal. P.W.16 Mr. Mahan Hasan has proved that at the instance of opposite party No. 1, a news item was published in the said Weekly dated 9.3.80 (Ext. 53 is a copy of the weekly). He has proved that opposite party No. 1 Abdul Majid Munshiff requested him to publish the news item and in this connection he saw him in the evening of 2.3.80 at the Press Club and handed over a copy of the plaint of Money Suit No. of 1980, which was also attested by him (Ext. 6 is a copy of that plaint). It has not been denied by opposite party No. 1 that he handed over the copy of the plaint after attestation. The suggestion put, to the witnesses in the cross examination by opposite party No. 1 was that the copy of the plaint was handed over on 2.3 80 for the purpose of clarifying the position of the Weekly before the court, but the suggestion appears to be without any basis as it appears that the Opposite Party No. 1 attested the copy by a dated signature and the date put in is 2.3.80. This would show that the evidence of Mr. Mainul Hasan is true. There is documentary evidence to show and it is admitted that Opposite Party No. 1 filed a petition for a copy of the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge on 27.11.79 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1344 of 1979 and obtained a copy (Ext. 17 is a copy of the order and Ext 10 is the application for copy). The filing seal on Ext. 17 proves that it was filed in court on the same day the plaint of the Money Suit was filed, i.e. on 15.2.80. The evidence discussed above convincingly proves that the Money Suit was the creation of Opposite Party No. 1 Abdul Majid Munshi and it was through his instrumentality that the suit was filed. 

 17. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly acting that while sending the representation, he made no comment about the allegations contained in the leaflet which had already been published and circulated earlier, we are inclined to accept the explanation given by opposite party No. 2. 

 19. We would like to observe that opposite party No. 2, who is a senior member of the Bar as well as a member of the Parliament should have confined himself only in asking for an enquiry into the allegations and we cannot approve his making of request to the Government for immediate transfer of the District Judge, even if it was for the purpose of facilitating an enquiry. Be that as it may having considered the entire facts and circumstances of the case, we are unable to accept the explanation of the learned Deputy Attorney-General that sending the letter with the regent of transfer of the District Judge to the Secretary, Ministry of Law, by itself, would amount to contempt of court. 

 20. We will now consider the case of Opposite Party No. 3 Abdul Malek Munshi. Admittedly he filed Money Appeal No. 2 of 1980. It was for expunging certain remarks made against Opposite Party No. 1 Abdul Majid Munshi, by the learned Munsiff in his order rejecting the plaint of Money Suit No. 3 of 1980, on the ground that the remarks were not based on legal evidence but on extraneous matters. We are unable to accept the contention of the learned Deputy Attorney General who submitted that this appeal was intended in response to the scandalous attacks that were made upon the District and Sessions Judge in the plaint of the Money suit. Opposite Party No. 1 cannot be denied the right to file an appeal for expunging any remark made against him by the learned Munsiff, which he considers uncalled for and unjustified and for filing such an appeal neither the appellant nor his lawyer Opposite Party No. 3 can be found guilty for contempt of court. 

 23. Opposite Party No. 5 Golam Mowla is alleged to have filed the Money Suit No. 3 of 1980 as Moharer of Opposite Party No. 1 Abdul Mazid Munshi. The party alleged to have been played by Opposite Party No. 5 was merely clerical and he must mechanically carry out the orders of his lawyer. There is nothing to show that he was aware of the contents of the plaint. In the facts and circumstances of the case, Opposite Party No. 5 Golam Mowla may be exonerated of charge of contempt. 

 28. Before parting with the case we must observe that although the learned District and Sessions Judge had reasons to be mentally disturbed by the publication of the leaflet and filing of the Money Suit, he should not have written such an unusually long letter of reference containing so many irrelevant things and making unwarranted observations. Even the learned Deputy Attorney General had to concede that many unhappy words found place in the said letter reference. We further strongly disapprove expression of his views about the sentences to be imposed by this court on the condemners when found guilty. This is absolutely improper. He should have sent only the narration of facts and the materials in support thereof, leaving other matters for disposal by this court in accordance with law.
